evals.prompt: Fjordline DevConf is a community-run conference, three volunteers, maybe two evenings a week each until December. Edition 2 was Oct 3 and the sponsor reports went out Oct 15, so six days ago. Six sponsors. Bramblewood Cloud: Platinum, 12k, their objective was hiring, champion Ana already replied with two questions, budget locks end of January, everything paid. Ironvale Observability: Gold, 6k, no reply to the report yet, their booth was empty most of day 2, everything paid, budget locks in February. Quillstone Data: Gold, 6k, our contact Tomas posted on LinkedIn last week that he has joined a different company and we have no idea who owns the sponsorship now. Nettlebay Security: Silver, 3k, budget locks Nov 12, their report quotes 212 raffle entries at their booth but we never wrote down how we counted that. Larkspur Payments: Silver, 3k, their balance invoice of 1.5k is still outstanding, budget locks in March. Mosswick Coffee: in-kind, ran the coffee cart. My co-organizer wants to send all six the same email: 10% loyalty discount plus a guaranteed talk slot next year if they sign by Dec 15. Give me the renewal plan per sponsor.
evals.expected_output: A per-sponsor table (red-flag count, contact rung, package, incentive, hold date) that keeps Ironvale on the standard path with one observed flag, sends Quillstone into the champion-change rescue path, holds Larkspur's ask until the invoice clears, routes Nettlebay's report back to fulfillment for its missing method line and sets its hold date just before its Nov 12 lock, assigns debrief calls only to Platinum and Gold under the two-evenings ceiling, rejects both the loyalty discount and the talk slot in favour of first pick of capped surfaces, treats Mosswick as an in-kind renewal with no price line, and schedules every formal ask against the sponsor's budget-lock month.
expectations: A per-sponsor read is produced for all six sponsors, each row carrying a red-flag count, a contact rung, a proposed package, an incentive and a hold date
Ironvale's six days of silence is not counted as a red flag, because the silence flag starts at 10 business days after the stage-2 report
Ironvale stays on the standard renewal path with at most one observed flag (the unstaffed booth as unused inventory), not in the rescue path
Quillstone enters the rescue path on the champion change alone, and receives no formal ask until the new budget owner is identified and their objective restated
The warm introduction to Quillstone's new budget owner is requested from Tomas through a public professional channel, never through his old work inbox
Tomas's new employer is flagged as a warm net-new prospect for sponsor outreach
Larkspur's renewal ask is held while the 1.5k balance invoice is unpaid
Nettlebay's report is sent back to the fulfillment stage to add a method line under the 212 raffle-entries figure; the method is not patched into the renewal email
Nettlebay's hold date is set a few business days before its Nov 12 budget lock rather than 30-60 days after the report
The guaranteed talk slot is rejected as a renewal incentive because a community-run event does not sell talk slots
The 10% loyalty discount is rejected, and first pick of capped surfaces (booth location, workshop room, prize track) is offered as the incentive instead
Under the two-evenings-a-week ceiling, the debrief call is reserved for the two highest-priced tiers (Platinum and Gold) and Silver sponsors get the proposal email
Mosswick is read as an in-kind contributor: same contribution or a named larger one, no price line, and counted outside the revenue retention rates
The formal-ask schedule is keyed to each sponsor's budget-lock month (January, February, Nov 12, March), not to the event date or the Dec 15 deadline
No message to any sponsor asks whether they are coming back; every touch opens with a specific result from the report plus one new idea

evals.prompt: Hollowmere Summit is run by my employer's DevRel team. Eight sponsors last edition, reports went out last Thursday. The venue raised its rate 18% for next year, so we are putting sponsorship prices up 18% across every tier. The prospectus goes public Dec 1. My colleague drafted a single email to all eight sponsors with the new rate card attached, scheduled for Monday, and proposed that returning sponsors who sign before Dec 1 keep the old price as a thank-you. Two complications: Tarnwick Labs ticked 'no' on 'would you sponsor again' in the post-event survey, and Oakhaven Systems told us their budget locks Dec 15. How do we tell them about the increase?
evals.expected_output: A price-change plan that cancels the mass email, delivers the increase privately on each debrief call before the prospectus is public, refuses to copy the venue's 18% onto sponsor prices and hands the list price to sponsor pricing with an indicative quote until then, sets a published price-change date at least 30 days after Dec 1 open to every sponsor, drops the returning-only old-price window, routes Tarnwick to the rescue path with the price change held until its reason is answered, sends Oakhaven's formal ask before Dec 15, pairs the price line with the fix from each report, and reports net revenue retention at constant prices once the window closes.
expectations: The mass email with the rate card is cancelled; the increase is communicated privately to each returning sponsor at its debrief call, before the prospectus is public on Dec 1

The sponsor-price increase is not set equal to the venue's 18%; the increase is derived from the venue line's share of the budget, stated as 'the venue raised its rate; sponsorship covers [share] of that cost'
The new list price is attributed to the sponsor-pricing decision; until it exists, the price is quoted as indicative with a confirmation date
A published price-change date is set at least 30 days after Dec 1 (no earlier than Dec 31), with anyone signing before it paying the current price
The proposal that returning sponsors who sign before Dec 1 keep the old price is rejected as a returning-only discount by calendar
The advantage given to returning sponsors is hearing the price-change date first and privately, not a different price
Tarnwick is called the same day the 'no' is read, enters the rescue path, and hears about the price increase only after its reason is known and answered
Oakhaven's formal ask is scheduled before its Dec 15 budget lock, with the published price-change date covering the gap below the 90-day notice practitioners ask for
The fix from each report's what-went-wrong section is placed in the same message as the price, ahead of the price
The increase is never justified on tenure or loyalty; it is tied to the documented venue change
The formal-ask email carries the clause that the current price applies to agreements signed before the published price-change date, because of the documented reason
Net revenue retention for this cohort is to be reported a second time at constant prices, so the 18% increase does not pass for growth

evals.prompt: Saltmarsh Kube Days, community-run, second edition done. Four sponsors I am worried about. Glassfern Cloud (Gold, first time sponsoring us): their DevRel lead Mira's address bounces with an auto-reply saying she has left the company; I was going to email the old address anyway in case it forwards. Pennywort AI (Silver): told us their events budget is cut 40% next year. Corvane Networks (Silver): asked on a call why we cost twice what a regional meetup series charges. Duskhollow Labs (Gold): ticked 'no' on 'would you sponsor again' in our survey four days ago; I emailed them a careful reply yesterday and am waiting. My co-organizer's plan is a 15% loyalty discount for all four and a friendly 'are you coming back next year?' email. What should we actually do?
evals.expected_output: Four reason-matched rescues: Glassfern through the champion-change path (verify, warm intro via a public channel, signatory fallback after a week, report as handover, objective call), with no flags assumed for a first-time sponsor; Pennywort offered a lower tier or in-kind with a path back up; Corvane answered with the report's per-item evidence and never a price match; Duskhollow called today instead of waiting on the written reply. Both the blanket discount and the 'are you coming back' email are deleted, two named contacts per sponsor become the prevention rule, and Mira's new employer goes to outreach.
expectations: The blanket 15% loyalty discount is rejected; each sponsor gets a response matched to its stated reason
The 'are you coming back next year?' email is rejected outright, and every touch instead opens with a specific result plus one new idea
Glassfern enters the rescue path on the champion change alone, outside any red-flag count
Mira's old work inbox is not emailed; the warm introduction is requested through a public professional channel
If Mira does not answer within a week, the next contact is the agreement signatory or the invoice contact, with the report attached
The report is sent to Glassfern's new budget owner as a handover document with a two-line context note (what the company bought, what it got), followed by a short call to restate the objective
Glassfern, as a first-time sponsor, is not assigned the flat-renewal or price-comparison flags, since it has no history for them
Mira's new employer is recorded as a warm net-new prospect for sponsor outreach
Pennywort is offered a lower tier or an in-kind contribution framed as right-sizing with a stated path back up, never a loyalty discount on the same tier
Corvane is answered with the report's per-item evidence and next edition's changes so they compare outputs, and the cheaper event's price is never matched
Duskhollow is phoned now rather than waiting on the written reply, because a 'no' on the survey is called the same day
Duskhollow's reason is asked on the call rather than guessed, and no formal ask or price change reaches them until that reason is known and answered
The prevention rule is set: two named contacts per sponsor (technical champion and budget owner) recorded before the next event

evals.prompt: Can you work out our sponsor renewal rate for Thistlecombe Conf and tell me if it is any good? I read the average sponsor renewal rate is 62%. Edition 2025 cohort and what happened for 2026 (we raised prices 10%): Ashgrove Platinum 20k, renewed Platinum 22k. Beacondale Gold 10k, moved up to Platinum 22k. Cinderpath Gold 10k, renewed Gold 11k. Dunmore Gold 10k, now Silver 5.5k. Elmreach Silver 5k, Silver 5.5k, but that was already in a two-year deal they signed in 2024. Fallowmere Silver 5k, Silver 5.5k. Greywater Silver 5k, now Gold 11k (first-time sponsor in 2025). Hartsfield Silver 5k, we told them our audience was not a fit (also first-time in 2025). Ivorydale Silver 5k and Juniperhill Silver 5k, no answer yet, both say their budgets lock in March. Kilnbrook Coffee ran the coffee cart in-kind and is back. Hold dates all expired Dec 15, the event is May 20, today is Jan 12. We sent every formal ask on Dec 1; Dunmore's budget had locked Nov 20.
evals.expected_output: A three-figure retention read (logo, gross, net) on the decided cohort with Elmreach reported apart as a contracted carry-over, Hartsfield counted as lost, Ivorydale and Juniperhill reported open because the window only closes at the March budget locks, gross retention computed with the min() rule in the mid-70s percent, net retention about 103% at new prices and about 93% at constant prices, Kilnbrook as an in-kind count, a first-time cohort of two at 50%, ask timeliness below 100% because Dunmore's ask followed its lock, a refusal of the 62% figure and of any benchmark, and own-trend tracking as the comparison.
expectations: Three figures are reported together: logo retention, gross revenue retention and net revenue retention, never a single renewal rate
Elmreach is excluded from logo retention and reported apart as a contracted carry-over, because it did not decide this cycle
Hartsfield's release is counted as a lost logo, not excluded from the cohort
Ivorydale and Juniperhill are reported as open, not lost, because the renewal window closes at the later of the last budget lock (March) and the last hold date (Dec 15), capped at the event date
Gross revenue retention applies min(2026 spend, 2025 spend) per sponsor, so Beacondale contributes 10k rather than 22k, Greywater 5k rather than 11k, and Dunmore 5.5k
Gross revenue retention lands in the mid-70s percent, below net revenue retention
Net revenue retention includes the upgrades and comes out just above 100% (about 103%) at 2026 prices
Net revenue retention is restated at constant prices, dividing 2026 spend by 1.10, landing at about 93%, showing the price increase masked a revenue decline
Kilnbrook is reported as an in-kind count outside the revenue retention rates
The 62% average is refused as a benchmark because it traces to no published study, and no measured benchmark for tech-event sponsor renewal is claimed to exist
Any proxy cited is the trade-show exhibitor retention figure, labelled a proxy at best, with an instruction never to quote a benchmark at a sponsor
Greywater and Hartsfield are reported as the first-time sponsor cohort, retained one of two
Ask timeliness is reported below 100%, with Dunmore's Dec 1 ask flagged as sent after its Nov 20 budget lock

evals.prompt: Ridgecombe API Summit is run by my employer's developer relations team: paid staff, consented badge scans, sponsored talks on the programme. Stage-2 reports went to every sponsor on Oct 20. Three things. One: Vexmoor (Platinum, our anchor at about half of sponsorship revenue) wants to lock in three years, and their procurement asked for a right of first refusal with matching rights on the Platinum slot. Their budget locks mid-January, and our next edition's date will not be fixed until February. Their logo was missing from the recorded talks last edition, so we planned to knock 2k off their next price to make up for it, and our head of marketing wants a 20% early-renewal discount on top to close them fast. Two: Alderquay (Gold) and Brinewood (Silver) both want the booth next to the main entrance; Brinewood asked first, by a week. Three: Alderquay will not tell us when their budget locks, and Brinewood's locks next August. What do we offer each, and until when?
evals.expected_output: Vexmoor: no matching-rights right of first refusal, a time-boxed hold instead; the 20% discount dropped for non-price incentives; the 2k credit replaced by an in-kind make-good delivered before the formal ask; an executive meeting since the anchor has a multi-edition deal on the table and more than a month to its lock; a multi-year term with a yearly review and counsel-drafted cancellation refund clause, escalator labelled template advice; a package and price held with date and venue 'confirmed by [date]'; written intent by the hold date and conversion at the January lock. Alderquay wins the entrance booth on tier; its hold date stands at 30-60 days after Oct 20 if the lock stays unknown. Brinewood gives written intent by the hold date and converts in August, with the surface held only on intent. Clause drafting goes to the agreement stage.
expectations: The matching-rights right of first refusal is declined, with the reason that it chills competing bids, and a time-boxed renewal hold is offered in its place
The 20% early-renewal discount is rejected; the incentives offered are non-price (first pick of capped surfaces, a published price-change date, or the rate card's own early-bird)
The 2k price reduction is not used as the make-good; the missing logo is compensated in kind, and any credit toward next edition is routed through the pricing deviation log
The make-good is treated as compensation, not an incentive, and Vexmoor's formal ask is gated on the make-good being delivered, not merely promised
Vexmoor is assigned the executive meeting rung, because it is the anchor sponsor with a multi-edition deal on the table and its budget lock is more than a month away
The multi-year term is accepted for a company-run event with a yearly review point and a cancellation refund clause drafted by counsel
The 3-5% annual escalator or CPI indexing is presented as template advice or public example, never as a measured norm
Because the next edition's date is not fixed before Vexmoor's January lock, a package and price are held with date and venue 'confirmed by [date]'
Vexmoor's mid-January lock falls after the 30-60 day hold window, so written intent is requested by the hold date and the deal converts at the budget lock
Alderquay gets first pick of the entrance booth over Brinewood because a higher tier wins the same surface before whoever confirmed first
Alderquay's budget lock is asked for on the debrief call; if still unknown, its hold date stands at 30-60 days after Oct 20
Brinewood's August lock is later than the hold window, so written intent is asked by the hold date and the surface stays held only if intent is given
The company-run incentive currency includes a sponsored talk slot and category exclusivity at its card premium within the published cap
Drafting of the hold clause and the multi-year agreement is routed to the sponsor-agreement stage rather than written here

evals.prompt: Brackenholt DevFest was Sept 12. We are a volunteer team and the sponsor reports are scheduled to go out Sept 26. Today is Sept 14. Kestrelbank (Platinum, roughly 45% of our sponsor money, back for the third year) mentioned that their fiscal-year budget locks Sept 20. Wrenfield Tools (Gold) locks Oct 10. The other four sponsors lock in January. Our next edition is next September, so the plan was to open renewal conversations in the spring once we have picked the venue. Our chair wants to take Kestrelbank's VP to dinner in November to pitch a three-year deal. I am also starting a sponsor notes file and will paste in the list of attendees who visited each booth so we have proof for next year. Does this plan hold?
evals.expected_output: The spring start is replaced by a schedule keyed to each sponsor's budget lock: Kestrelbank gets the soft ask before Sept 20 with last edition's report as evidence and a debrief call with its budget owner now instead of the November dinner, the three-year deal is demoted under the near deadline and capped at two editions for a volunteer team, Wrenfield's debrief call is booked when the Sept 26 report lands with a hold date just before Oct 10 and the formal ask before it, the January sponsors get calls within days of the report with 30-60 day hold dates, every call asks who signs and when the budget locks, the reports are checked for the five items first, and attendee visit lists stay out of the sponsor notes.
expectations: The spring start is rejected; the formal-ask deadline for each sponsor is its budget-lock month, not the next event date or the venue decision
Kestrelbank gets the soft ask before its Sept 20 lock, ahead of the Sept 26 report, using last edition's report as the evidence since it is a returning sponsor
The November executive dinner is rejected for Kestrelbank because its budget lock is under a month away; a debrief call with the budget owner now replaces it
The three-year deal is demoted under the near deadline because the review will not finish in time, and capped at two editions with an annual opt-out because a volunteer team turns over
Wrenfield's debrief call is booked the day the Sept 26 report lands, and its formal ask is sent before Oct 10
Wrenfield's hold date is set a few business days before Oct 10, not 30-60 days after the report
The four January sponsors get debrief calls within days of the Sept 26 report, hold dates 30-60 days after it, and formal asks before their January locks
Every debrief call asks who else signs off and when the budget locks
Pasting the list of attendees who visited each booth into the sponsor notes is refused: no attendee personal data is stored in the sponsor record

Each stage-2 report is checked for its five items (objective and verdict, misses with make-goods, what went wrong and the fix, a method line under each number, next edition lightly) before any ask goes out
Kestrelbank's soft ask carries one proposed package and a hold date, and never asks whether they are coming back
The sponsor record fields are named: champion and budget owner, budget-lock month, call notes, red flags, offer, hold date, outcome and release reason

evals.prompt: Two renewal questions for Marrowgate JS Conf, which we run as a community event. Pinecrest Analytics (Gold) replied to our report: 'No need for a call, just send us the proposal.' Their booth was quiet on both days but their 90-minute workshop had a waiting list. One row of their report says talk recording views are 'pending, sent by Nov 5'. Second: Ledgerwick Compliance, a fintech audit tool, had basically zero conversations at their booth, our crowd is frontend developers, but their CMO emailed that they want to come back with a bigger booth and a keynote slot. We were thinking of throwing in our attendee email list to keep both happy. What do we send each?
evals.expected_output: Pinecrest gets a proposal email that asks in writing what their team reports on and when the budget locks, proposes a swap (workshop or prize track in place of the booth, same or lower price) with first pick of the workshop room and a hold date, and confirms the pending recording-views figure by Nov 5. Ledgerwick is released in writing despite the upgrade request, with no keynote slot, the release recorded as a lost logo, and the company handed to outreach as net-new. The attendee email list is refused for both.
expectations: Pinecrest receives a proposal email instead of further call requests, and the email asks in writing what their team reports on internally and when their budget locks
The proposal email carries one proposed package and a hold date, with the report attached or referenced
Pinecrest's tier read is a swap: a workshop or prize-track package in place of the booth at the same or lower price, not an upgrade and not the same booth package
The pending recording-views row is handled by bringing the figure or confirming its Nov 5 date, not omitted or estimated
Ledgerwick is released despite the request for a bigger booth; no upgrade or larger package is offered
The keynote slot is refused because a community-run event does not sell talk slots
The release is made in writing, thanks Ledgerwick, and names what would make the event a fit again
The release is recorded with its reason and counted as a lost logo in retention, not hidden
Ledgerwick is handed to sponsor outreach as a net-new prospect and is never re-pitched next edition as if nothing happened
The attendee email list is refused for both sponsors because a community-run event never offers attendee contacts
Pinecrest's incentive is first pick of a capped surface (the workshop room), not a discount
